summary: Raia Hadsell opens by introducing her 13-year journey at DeepMind, from philosophy undergraduate to PhD work on neural networks with Yann LeCun, to joining DeepMind's ~30-40 person team working on Atari, Go, StarCraft, and robotics. Now as VP overseeing ~1,200 scientists and engineers across 10 labs, she focuses on Frontier AI for Gemini's next architectures and problems only AI can address. DeepMind's approach targets root-node problems rather than leaf nodes, partnering broadly to enable downstream impact, guided by the mission of building AI responsibly for humanity's benefit. She presents three non-LLM innovation areas. First, advanced embedding models: inspired by neuroscience's Jennifer Aniston cells that activate across modalities for fast retrieval and recognition, DeepMind released Gemini Embeddings 2, a fully omnimodal model derived from Gemini that encodes text (8K tokens), 128 seconds of video, 80 seconds of audio, and full PDFs into unified semantic vectors using contrastive losses and Matryoshka representation learning for flexible dimensionality. Second, AI weather forecasting: starting from a Met Office challenge to predict rainfall better than physics models, DeepMind developed GraphCast (spherical graph neural network, 15-day forecasts, 100 atmospheric variables, accurately predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall 9 days out vs 6 for physics models), GenCast (probabilistic, more accurate 97% of the time vs benchmarks, 15-day forecast in 8 minutes on a single chip), and FGN (directly predicts cyclone behavior, used by US National Hurricane Center). Third, world models: emerging from game and simulation work, DeepMind developed Genie 1 (interactive 2D platformers, ran only a few seconds), Genie 2 (3D environments but not real-time and lacked real-world quality), and Genie 3 (high-quality, interactive, real-time 3D worlds with memory, consistency, and dynamic prompting). Genie 3 demonstrations include walking down a muddy lane in Kent with a visible body, skiing, flying through an artist-created world prompted from a video fragment, an origami lizard world with persistent memory allowing return to unchanged starting conditions, and real-time world modification while walking down the Camden Canal. Hadsell envisions applications in entertainment, adversarial multiplayer world-prompting, and education through immersive learning environments.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.summary: Hadsell introduces herself as a 13-year DeepMind veteran and UK AI Ambassador, tracing her career from philosophy of religion through PhD work on convolutional networks with Yann LeCun, to joining DeepMind's small team working on Atari, Go, StarCraft, and robotics. She now oversees ~1,200 scientists across 10 labs, focusing on Frontier AI for Gemini.

sections.title: DeepMind's Approach to Frontier AI
sections.summary: DeepMind targets root-node problems rather than leaf nodes, partnering broadly to enable downstream impact. The mission is building AI responsibly for humanity's benefit. Hadsell frames her talk around innovations beyond standard language models.

sections.title: Advanced Embedding Models and Gemini Embeddings 2
sections.summary: Hadsell explains Jennifer Aniston cells from neuroscience as inspiration for embedding models that enable fast retrieval and recognition across modalities. She introduces Gemini Embeddings 2, a fully omnimodal model derived from Gemini that encodes text, video, audio, and PDFs into unified semantic vectors using contrastive losses and Matryoshka representation learning for flexible dimensionality.

sections.title: AI for Weather Forecasting
sections.summary: Starting from a Met Office rainfall prediction challenge, DeepMind developed three weather models: GraphCast (spherical graph neural network, 15-day forecasts, 100 variables, accurately predicted Hurricane Lee 9 days out vs 6 for physics models), GenCast (probabilistic, 97% accuracy vs benchmarks, 8-minute forecasts on single chip), and FGN (directly predicts cyclone behavior, used by US National Hurricane Center).

sections.title: World Models and Genie Progression
sections.summary: Hadsell traces the evolution of Genie world models. Genie 1 generated interactive 2D platformers but ran only a few seconds. Genie 2 scaled to 3D games but was not real-time and lacked real-world quality. Genie 3 produces high-quality, interactive, real-time 3D worlds with memory, consistency, and dynamic prompting. Demonstrations include walking down a muddy lane in Kent with a visible body, skiing, flying through an artist-created world prompted from video, an origami lizard world with persistent memory, and real-time world modification while walking the Camden Canal. Hadsell envisions applications in entertainment, adversarial world-prompting, and immersive education.

demonstrations: GraphCast prediction of Hurricane Lee showing 9-day movement from Atlantic through landfall in Nova Scotia
Genie 1 generating 2D platformer game environments responsive to left/right user input
Genie 3 generating a muddy lane in Kent where the user has a visible body and can walk through water
Genie 3 world prompted from an artist's video fragment, allowing flight through and interaction with the created structure
Genie 3 origami lizard world demonstrating memory by returning to unchanged starting conditions after running in one direction
Genie 3 Camden Canal world dynamically modified in real-time through user prompting
limitations: Genie 1 could only run for a few seconds
Genie 2 was interactive but not real-time, requiring slow movement, and could not produce real-world quality or high-definition 3D environments
